title: Replace text status labels with icons where possible
description: For quick at-a-glance scanning (and to shrink the amount of text that needs translating/fitting in both Hindi and English per LODGY-30), replace text-only indicators with icon-first representations wherever a clear, unambiguous icon exists - bed vacant/occupied state, invoice status, tenant status. Pairs directly with LODGY-36's RAG color system: icon + color together, never color alone (already the app's convention per LODGY-31/57-style safety patterns), so this isn't about removing text for accessibility's sake, just making text secondary to a symbol that reads the same in either language.
acceptanceCriteria: Bed vacant/occupied indicators (BedGridScreen, VacantViewScreen) lead with an icon, with the RAG color from LODGY-36, text label present but secondary (e.g. smaller, or icon-with-tooltip) rather than the primary way status is conveyed
Invoice and tenant status badges (Unpaid/Partial/Paid, Active/Vacated) get a consistent icon per state, not just a colored chip with text

No status is ever conveyed by icon or color alone without a text label still available somewhere (for accessibility/screen readers and for anyone unfamiliar with the icon set) - this reduces reliance on translated text, it doesn't remove the translation entirely
Icon set is consistent with the app's existing stroke-icon style (ui/icons/CommonIcons.kt)

history.note: Added alongside the LODGY-36 color-coding rework: pairing icons with the new RAG colors so status reads at a glance and doesn't lean entirely on translated text.

Starting - adding a per-state stroke icon in ui/icons/StatusIcons.kt and threading it through the StatusBadge LODGY-36 just introduced, so icon and RAG colour arrive together at every call site and the text label stays present rather than being replaced.

Added ui/icons/StatusIcons.kt (BedVacant/BedOccupied/Check/Half/Alert/Exit, all built with the existing strokeIcon helper so they match the app's stroke set) and a matching .icon extension next to LODGY-36's .level, so a state's colour and symbol are decided in the same place. StatusBadge now takes the icon, draws it ahead of the text, and passes the label as the icon's contentDescription - the text is never removed, so screen readers and anyone unfamiliar with the symbol still get it, and no status is icon- or colour-only. Converted: invoice status chips, tenant status badges (directory + profile), VacantViewScreen rows, and BedGridScreen tiles where the label is demoted to labelSmall beside a leading icon. StatusLevelTest extended to assert each state has a distinct icon. testDebugUnitTest green.

PASS - all four. AC1: bed status leads with an icon on both BedGridScreen and VacantViewScreen - distinct occupied-bed and empty-bed glyphs carrying the LODGY-36 RAG colour, with the VACANT/OCCUPIED text present but secondary (smaller, and after the icon). AC2: consistent icon per state everywhere - invoices use Alert / Half / Check for Unpaid / Partial / Paid, tenants use Check for ACTIVE and Exit for VACATED, all mapped once in ui/common/StatusTokens.kt rather than per screen. AC3: nothing is icon- or colour-only - every badge still renders its text label, and the icons carry contentDescription (they surfaced as [VACANT]/[OCCUPIED]/[Paid]/[ACTIVE] in the accessibility tree), so screen readers and anyone unfamiliar with the icon set are covered. AC4: style is consistent - StatusIcons and CommonIcons are both built with the same shared strokeIcon() helper (24dp, stroke-only, no fill), so the new status glyphs match the existing set exactly.
